title: Exception hierarchy
hook: Everything hangs off System.Exception. The skill is choosing what a worker swallows, what it retries, and what it lets kill the message versus the process.

sections.heading: Types you actually name
sections.prose: SystemException is a historical bucket; you catch more specific types: ArgumentException (and ArgumentNullException, ArgumentOutOfRangeException), InvalidOperationException, IOException, HttpRequestException, JsonException, OperationCanceledException, TimeoutException. ApplicationException is obsolete as a policy. Custom exceptions should be rare, serializable in spirit (message + inner), and named for the domain (LeaseExpiredException), not for every if.

sections.heading: Worker versus bubble
sections.prose: An SQS or RabbitMQ consumer is a boundary. At HandleAsync you may catch known transient faults, retry, then fail the message to a DLQ. Unknown failures should bubble to the host so visibility stays honest — metrics, poison-message counts, process health. Catching Exception, logging, and returning as success is silent data loss. Static constructors that throw become TypeInitializationException wrapping the inner cause; you cannot “retry” that type in-process without unloading. High-concurrency submit paths should fail fast on cancellation and on invariant breaks, not wrap every call in Exception.

snippets.label: Message boundary: retry known, bubble unknown
snippets.explanation: Timeout is a known worker failure: log and rethrow so the queue infrastructure retries. There is no catch (Exception). Argument bugs bubble untouched.

sections.heading: Process-level facts
sections.prose: If no catch exists, the thread dies. In ASP.NET or a Worker Service the host may crash or log depending on configuration — still not a reason to catch everything. Unobserved Task exceptions used to crash processes on later .NET; the modern default logs them. That policy is module 13. Finalizer exceptions abort the finalizer — module 14.

interviewTakeaways: Catch specific types; Exception only at a true boundary.
Workers: retry/DLQ policy versus bubble. Do not succeed after a swallowed failure.
TypeInitializationException means the type is done for this process.
commonPitfalls: catch (Exception) { return; } in an SQS handler.
Custom exception types that add no extra data and are never caught by name.

jsTsCorrelations.note: JS has Error, TypeError, and user subclasses, but many libraries throw plain objects. C# culture is a real hierarchy under Exception.
TS cannot exhaustively type thrown errors. C# catch lists are the closest thing to an exhaustive failure story.
